mentions.name: EMIS Framework
mentions.description: A theoretical framework (EMIS, Energy–Matter–Information-Spacetime) that models the economy as a constrained 2D energy manifold where money is a bookkeeping layer over energy allocation. It combines a 2D manifold hypothesis reframing growth, inflation, and inequality as curvature problems, a Jackiw–Teitelboim-gravity analogy treating policy as boundary condition manipulation, a holographic mapping from boundary-level micro-transactions to bulk macroeconomic structure, and random-matrix statistics for crises, bubbles, and phase shifts. Work in progress includes formalizing the action functional, defining the admissible ensemble boundary for economic random matrix theory, and building a small simulation engine to test curvature versus liquidity stress.
mentions.problem: Attempts to dissolve the 100-year micro vs macro divide in economics by treating macro structure as emerging from discrete micro-transactions, and to unify economics with complex systems physics as a compression model for macro indicators and a path toward AI-native economic modeling.
mentions.audience: Theoretical physicists and quantitative finance practitioners, sought for feedback on the gravity mapping and RMT edge cases
